source_assumption_differences: Chewi, Lectures on Optimization, arXiv:2605.07006v1, §1.1 (https://arxiv.org/html/2605.07006v1#S1.SS1) supplies the black-box model with exact value and gradient and unrestricted local computation. This exercise specializes it to one real dimension, one deterministic query, fixed curvature and radius bounds, and a separate variant supplying the optimum value.

Chewi §4.1, Lemma 4.2 (https://arxiv.org/html/2605.07006v1#S4.SS1) is an algorithmic reduction using regularization of a general convex smooth objective about an initial point; it also analyzes approximation, distance, and complexity. The local declaration elaborates only the regularization's analytic properties and allows delta=0. The exercise instead uses a constant base and its regularization center is the unknown minimizer of the resulting quadratic.

Chewi §4.2 (https://arxiv.org/html/2605.07006v1#S4.SS2) treats dimension-dependent iteration lower bounds for deterministic gradient-span algorithms. Its exercises extend that construction to a distance bound or a direct strongly convex chain example. The packet's arbitrary-query scalar pair, explicit 1/64 threshold, freely chosen offsets, and known-optimum recovery are a separate original benchmark exercise, not a numbered exercise or a theorem transferred from §4.
